```d
    assert(pressure > 0.deg && pressure <= 30.deg, "the pressure angle goes from above 0° to 30° (20° is the "
        ~ "standard, 14.5° and 25° the others): not $(pressure)");
}

/// A spur gear standing on z = 0, with an optional bore; `steps` points on
/// each flank's involute and as many on its root (more: smoother teeth,
/// slower). Tags: the axis "gears.axis", the bore's wall "gears.bore".
Solid spurGear(Length m, int teeth, Length thickness, Length bore = 0.mm, Angle pressure = 20.deg,
    Length backlash = 0.1.mm, int steps = 6)
{
    assert(bore < rootDiameter(m, teeth) - 2 * m, "spurGear: the bore must be smaller than the gear's root circle, with a module of material left");
    auto g = gearProfile(m, teeth, pressure, backlash, steps).extrude(thickness);
    if (bore > 0.mm)
        g -= cylinder(d: bore, h: 3 * thickness, center: true)
            .addTag("gears.bore", recursive: true);
    return g.addTag("gears.axis", at: axis(origin: vec(0.mm, 0.mm, 0.mm), direction: Z));
}

/// A straight rack along +X starting at x = 0, teeth up, pitch line at y = 0;
/// backlash thins the teeth on the pitch line, as on a gear. Tag: the pitch
/// line "gears.pitch" (an axis along it, on the rack's bottom face).
Solid rack(Length m, int teeth, Length thickness, Length base = 0.mm, Angle pressure = 20.deg,
    Length backlash = 0.1.mm)
{
    assert(teeth >= 1, "a rack needs at least 1 tooth");
    checkPressure(pressure);
    immutable e = backlash / 2;
    immutable p = PI * m;
    immutable b = base > 0.mm ? base : 2 * m;
    immutable t = tan(pressure);

    // the tooth's top keeps some width
    immutable most = p / 2 - 2 * m * t;
    assert(backlash >= 0.mm && backlash < most, "rack: the backlash goes from 0 to under $(most) (the width "
        ~ "of the teeth's tops)");
    Vec2[] pts = [vec(0.mm, -1.25 * m - b)];
    foreach (k; 0 .. teeth)
    {
        immutable x0 = k * p;
        pts ~= [vec(x0, -1.25 * m), vec(x0 + p / 4 - 1.25 * m * t + e, -1.25 * m), vec(x0 + p / 4 + m * t + e, m),
                vec(x0 + 3 * p / 4 - m * t - e, m), vec(x0 + 3 * p / 4 + 1.25 * m * t - e, -1.25 * m)];
    }
    pts ~= [vec(teeth * p, -1.25 * m), vec(teeth * p, -1.25 * m - b)];
    return polygon(pts)
        .extrude(thickness)
        .addTag("gears.pitch", at: axis(origin: vec(0.mm, 0.mm, 0.mm), direction: X));
}
```

## Library source: hinges

```d
module hinges;

/// The two leaves of a hinge, printed in place: they come out of the
/// printer already joined and turn around the X axis. Tags: both leaves
/// carry the axis they turn round, "hinges.axis"; pinHinge's holes for the
/// pin are tagged "hinges.pin".
struct Hinge
{
    Solid fixed;    /// the leaf on -Y, with the pin
    Solid moving;   /// the leaf on +Y, turning around the pin
}

/// A print-in-place hinge along X, centred on the origin, leaves lying flat
/// on z = 0 and the axis at z = thickness. `knuckles` alternate between
/// the leaves (odd numbers keep it symmetric).
Hinge hinge(Length length = 40.mm, Length width = 15.mm, Length thickness = 3.mm, int knuckles = 5,
    Length clearance = 0.4.mm)
{
    assert(knuckles >= 3, "a hinge needs at least 3 knuckles");
    immutable outer = 2 * thickness;           // knuckle diameter
    immutable pin = outer * 0.45;
    immutable segment = length / knuckles;

    /// Knuckle i with the web that joins it to its leaf (side -1 or +1).
    Solid knuckle(int i, int side)
    {
        immutable x0 = -length / 2 + i * segment + (i > 0 ? clearance / 2 : 0.mm);
        immutable x1 = -length / 2 + (i + 1) * segment - (i < knuckles - 1 ? clearance / 2 : 0.mm);
        immutable reach = outer / 2 + clearance;
        auto web = box(x1 - x0, reach, thickness).move(x: (x0 + x1) / 2, y: side * reach / 2);
        return cylinder(d: outer, h: x1 - x0).rotate(y: 90).move(x: x0, z: thickness) + web;
    }

    Solid a = box(length, width, thickness).move(y: -width / 2 - outer / 2 - clearance);
    Solid b = box(length, width, thickness).move(y: width / 2 + outer / 2 + clearance);
    foreach (i; 0 .. knuckles)
    {
        if (i % 2 == 0)
            a += knuckle(i, -1);
        else
            b += knuckle(i, 1);
    }
    // the pin belongs to the fixed leaf and runs through the moving knuckles with clearance
    a += cylinder(d: pin, h: length - 2 * clearance).rotate(y: 90).move(x: -length / 2 + clearance, z: thickness);
    foreach (i; 0 .. knuckles)
        if (i % 2 == 1)
            b -= cylinder(d: pin + 2 * clearance, h: length).rotate(y: 90).move(x: -length / 2, z: thickness);
    return leaves(a, b, thickness);
}

/// The two leaves, each with the axis they turn round (along X at z = thickness).
private Hinge leaves(Solid a, Solid b, Length thickness)
{
    auto turn = axis(origin: vec(0.mm, 0.mm, thickness), direction: X);
    return Hinge(a.addTag("hinges.axis", at: turn), b.addTag("hinges.axis", at: turn));
}

/// A living hinge: two plates `width` wide each, lying flat side by side
/// along X, joined by a thin web `web` thick and `gap` wide at their
/// underside, which bends. For PETG, PP or TPU (PLA cracks after a few
/// bends); print it flat, the web on the bed, so its layers run across the
/// fold. The plates lie on -Y and +Y, the fold line along X at y = 0.
Solid livingHinge(Length length = 40.mm, Length width = 15.mm, Length thickness = 3.mm, Length web = 0.5.mm,
    Length gap = 3.mm)
{
    assert(web < thickness, "livingHinge: the web must be thinner than the plates");
    auto plates = box(length, width, thickness).move(y: -width / 2 - gap / 2)
        + box(length, width, thickness).move(y: width / 2 + gap / 2);
    return plates + box(length, gap + 2.mm, web);
}

/// The knuckles of a hinge along X round the axis at z = thickness, each with
/// its web to its leaf, for leaf `side` (-1 or +1), as hinge() makes them.
private Solid knuckleOf(int i, int side, Length length, Length thickness, int knuckles, Length clearance)
{
    immutable outer = 2 * thickness, segment = length / knuckles;
    immutable x0 = -length / 2 + i * segment + (i > 0 ? clearance / 2 : 0.mm);
    immutable x1 = -length / 2 + (i + 1) * segment - (i < knuckles - 1 ? clearance / 2 : 0.mm);
    immutable reach = outer / 2 + clearance;
    auto web = box(x1 - x0, reach, thickness).move(x: (x0 + x1) / 2, y: side * reach / 2);
    return cylinder(d: outer, h: x1 - x0).rotate(y: 90).move(x: x0, z: thickness) + web;
}

/// A hinge turning on a separate pin: the knuckles of both leaves holed
/// `pin` + 2 × `clearance` across, for a length of 1.75 mm filament, a nail or
/// a screw pushed through when assembled. Laid as hinge() lays its leaves (the
/// axis along X at z = thickness); the leaves print apart, flat, and the
/// hinge comes apart again.
Hinge pinHinge(Length length = 40.mm, Length width = 15.mm, Length thickness = 3.mm, int knuckles = 5,
    Length pin = 1.75.mm, Length clearance = 0.3.mm)
{
    assert(knuckles >= 3, "a hinge needs at least 3 knuckles");
    assert(pin < 1.6 * thickness, "pinHinge: the pin is too thick for the knuckles: thicker leaves");
    immutable outer = 2 * thickness;
    Solid a = box(length, width, thickness).move(y: -width / 2 - outer / 2 - clearance);
    Solid b = box(length, width, thickness).move(y: width / 2 + outer / 2 + clearance);
    foreach (i; 0 .. knuckles)
    {
        if (i % 2 == 0)
            a += knuckleOf(i, -1, length, thickness, knuckles, clearance);
        else
            b += knuckleOf(i, 1, length, thickness, knuckles, clearance);
    }
    auto bore = cylinder(d: pin + 2 * clearance, h: length + 2.mm)
        .rotate(y: 90)
        .move(x: -length / 2 - 1.mm, z: thickness)
        .addTag("hinges.pin", recursive: true);
    return leaves(a - bore, b - bore, thickness);
}

/// A hinge that snaps together: three knuckles, the two outer ones on the
/// fixed leaf with a cone standing in from each, the middle one on the
/// moving leaf with a conical socket at each end. Spring the outer knuckles
/// apart a little, push the middle one between them, and the cones click into
/// their sockets; it comes apart the same way. Laid as hinge() lays its
/// leaves; they print apart, flat.
Hinge snapHinge(Length length = 30.mm, Length width = 15.mm, Length thickness = 3.mm, Length clearance = 0.3.mm)
{
    immutable outer = 2 * thickness, segment = length / 3;
    Solid a = box(length, width, thickness).move(y: -width / 2 - outer / 2 - clearance)
        + knuckleOf(0, -1, length, thickness, 3, clearance) + knuckleOf(2, -1, length, thickness, 3, clearance);
    Solid b = box(length, width, thickness).move(y: width / 2 + outer / 2 + clearance)
        + knuckleOf(1, 1, length, thickness, 3, clearance);

    // the cones: from the outer knuckles' inner faces towards the middle, 45° so they print and snap
    immutable cd = 0.6 * outer, ch = cd / 2 * 0.8;
    auto cone1 = cone(d1: cd, d2: cd - 2 * ch, h: ch).rotate(y: 90);
    immutable inner0 = -length / 2 + segment - clearance / 2, inner1 = length / 2 - segment + clearance / 2;
    a = a + cone1.move(x: inner0, z: thickness) + cone1.mirror(X).move(x: inner1, z: thickness);
    auto socket = cone(d1: cd + 2 * clearance, d2: cd - 2 * ch + 2 * clearance, h: ch + clearance).rotate(y: 90);
    b = b - socket.move(x: inner0 - 0.01.mm, z: thickness) - socket.mirror(X).move(x: inner1 + 0.01.mm, z: thickness);
    return leaves(a, b, thickness);
}
```

## Library source: snaps

```d
module snaps;

/// Cantilever snap-fit hooks. The hook stands on z = 0 and leans out along
/// +X; print it standing so the layers run along the beam.

/// A hook: a flexible beam `length` long with a barb `overhang` deep at the
/// top. `lead` is the slope that pushes it aside when inserting.
Solid snapHook(Length length = 10.mm, Length thickness = 1.5.mm, Length width = 5.mm, Length overhang = 1.mm,
    Angle lead = 30.deg)
{
    assert(lead >= 5.deg && lead <= 85.deg, "snapHook: the lead is the slope of the barb's face, from 5° (long "
        ~ "and gentle) to 85° (short and steep): not $(lead)");
    immutable barb = overhang / tan(lead);     // height of the sloped face
    auto profile = polygon([vec(0.mm, 0.mm), vec(thickness, 0.mm), vec(thickness, length),
                            vec(thickness + overhang, length), vec(thickness, length + barb),
                            vec(0.mm, length + barb)]);
    // drawn in the XY plane (y up the beam), then stood up
    return profile.extrude(width).move(z: -width / 2).rotate(x: 90).move(y: 0.mm);
}

/// The slot a hook clicks into, to subtract from the mating wall: a window
/// round the beam, `clearance` larger, with room on the -X side for the beam
/// to bend aside while the barb goes through; then the barb rests on the
/// wall beyond the window's +X edge.
Solid snapSlot(Length thickness = 1.5.mm, Length width = 5.mm, Length overhang = 1.mm, Length wall = 2.mm,
    Length clearance = 0.3.mm) =>
    box(thickness + overhang + 2 * clearance, width + 2 * clearance, wall + 1.mm)
        .move(x: (thickness - overhang) / 2, z: -0.5.mm);
```

## Library source: enclosures

```d
module enclosures;

import std.hardware : Screw, M3, hole;

/// Boxes with rounded corners and enclosures with lids.
///
/// Tags: a tray's or a base's rim, where the lid rests, is tagged
/// "enclosures.rim", its floor inside "enclosures.floor"; the lip, the ring
/// between a base and its lid, "enclosures.lip".

/// A box centred in X and Y on z = 0, with vertical edges rounded by `r`.
Solid roundedBox(Length x, Length y, Length z, Length r = 3.mm)
{
    assert(r > 0.mm && 2 * r < min(x, y), "roundedBox: r must be more than 0 and less than half the shorter side");
    return box(x, y, z).fillet(edges.parallel(Z), r: r);
}

/// An open box: walls `wall` thick, open on top.
Solid tray(Length x, Length y, Length z, Length wall = 2.mm, Length r = 3.mm)
{
    assert(wall > 0.mm && 2 * wall < min(x, y) && wall < z, "tray: the wall must be thinner than half the box and its height");
    // a wall as thick as the corners' radius leaves the inside corners a radius of nothing
    assert(abs(wall - r) > 0.05.mm, "tray: a wall as thick as r leaves sharp inside corners that cannot be built: "
        ~ "make r larger than the wall (or the wall thicker than r)");
    auto t = roundedBox(x, y, z, r).shell(open: faces.top, thickness: wall);
    t.faces.top.addTag("enclosures.rim");
    t.faces.normal(Z).filter(f => abs(f.center.z - wall) < 0.001.mm).addTag("enclosures.floor");
    return t;
}

/// A base and a lid that fit together, both standing on z = 0.
struct Enclosure
{
    Solid base;
    Solid lid;
}

/// An enclosure with `inner` free space (x, y, z), a lid with a lip that
/// fits inside the base, and a screw post in each corner.
Enclosure enclosure(Vec3 inner, Length wall = 2.mm, Length r = 3.mm, Length lidHeight = 4.mm,
    Screw screw = M3, Length clearance = 0.2.mm)
{
    assert(lidHeight > 0.mm && lidHeight < inner.z, "enclosure: the lid's lip (lidHeight) must be lower than the inside (inner.z)");
    immutable ox = inner.x + 2 * wall, oy = inner.y + 2 * wall;
    auto base = tray(ox, oy, inner.z + wall, wall, r);
    auto lid = roundedBox(ox, oy, wall, r);
    // the lip: a thin ring that slides into the base
    immutable lx = inner.x - 2 * clearance, ly = inner.y - 2 * clearance;
    auto lip = roundedBox(lx, ly, lidHeight, max(r - wall, 0.5.mm)) - roundedBox(lx - 2 * wall, ly - 2 * wall, lidHeight * 3,
        max(r - 2 * wall, 0.5.mm)).move(z: -lidHeight);
    lid += lip.move(z: wall).addTag("enclosures.lip", recursive: true);

    // posts: tapped for the screw in the base, clearance holes in the lid.
    // The screw's axis is as near the corner as it can be: its hole keeps
    // 1.2 mm of wall outside it, across the rounded corner too, and its head
    // stays on the lid. With thick walls the axis is inside the wall and the
    // post all but disappears into the corner
    immutable postR = screw.tap / 2 + screw.d * 0.8;
    immutable keep = max(screw.tap / 2 + 1.2.mm, screw.head / 2 + 0.5.mm);   // from the axis to the outside
    // the axis' distance from the inner faces (negative: inside the walls)
    auto inset = keep - wall;
    if (keep > r)
        inset = max(inset, r - wall);
    else
        inset = max(inset, r - wall - (r - keep) / sqrt(2.0));
    immutable px = inner.x / 2 - inset, py = inner.y / 2 - inset;
    // up to the rim, where the lid rests: the screw bites from the lid on (the lip is notched round
    // each post, below); a short screw holds, one lid's thickness and a few mm into the post
    immutable postH = inner.z + wall;
    // from the axis to the middle of the walls: the post is one piece with
    // the corner it stands in, with no gap behind it
    immutable reach = inset + wall / 2;
    foreach (sx; [-1, 1])
        foreach (sy; [-1, 1])
        {
            auto post = cylinder(r: postR, h: postH);
            if (reach > 0.1.mm)
                post += box(reach, reach, postH).move(x: sx * reach / 2, y: sy * reach / 2);
            // near the corner the post would stick out: trimmed by the box's outside
            base += post.move(x: sx * px, y: sy * py) & roundedBox(ox, oy, postH, r);
            // from the rim (the screw may go through the wall) down to the floor
            base -= hole(screw, inner.z, "tap").move(x: sx * px, y: sy * py, z: inner.z + wall);
            lid -= cylinder(d: screw.clearance, h: 10 * wall, center: true).move(x: sx * px, y: sy * py);
            // room for the post in the lip, the clearance all round it; the
            // square reaches past the lip, which stops short of the corner
            immutable out = max(inset, 0.mm) + wall + clearance;
            auto room = cylinder(r: postR + clearance, h: lidHeight * 2)
                + box(out, out, lidHeight * 2).move(x: sx * out / 2, y: sy * out / 2);
            lid -= room.move(x: sx * px, y: sy * py, z: wall);
        }
    return Enclosure(base, lid);
}

/// A case with upright walls round one part: the shadow it casts on the
/// plane `on` (the ground, XY, unless given), its convex hull grown by
/// `clearance`, walls `wall` thick standing square to the plane, so the part
/// drops in along the plane's normal and lifts out. Base and lid meet at
/// `split` of the part's height (halfway unless given): opened, the part
/// stands out of the base, to take it. The base: a floor `wall` thick under
/// the part, its walls, and a lip `lip` high rising from their inner half;
/// the lid: its walls, `play` wider round the lip, and a top `wall` thick
/// `clearance` over the part. close: "lip" holds the lid on by friction;
/// "snap" adds a bead round the lip, halfway up it, that clicks into a groove
/// inside the lid (its wall gives a little as it goes over). The lip is 3 mm
/// high unless given, lower on a flat part (a card, a coin, a board) where
/// that does not fit under the lid's top.
///
/// Tags: the base's floor inside is "enclosures.floor", the top of its walls,
/// where the lid rests, "enclosures.rim", the lip (on the base) "enclosures.lip";
/// the lid has none.
Enclosure shadowCase(Solid inside, Plane on = XY, Length wall = 2.mm, Length clearance = 0.5.mm,
    double split = 0.5, string close = "lip", Length lip = 0.mm, Length play = 0.2.mm)
{
    assert(close == "lip" || close == "snap", "shadowCase: close is \"lip\" or \"snap\", not \"" ~ close ~ "\"");
    assert(wall > 0.mm && clearance >= 0.mm && lip >= 0.mm && play >= 0.mm && play < wall,
        "shadowCase: a wall and a lip thicker than 0, a clearance and a play of 0 or more (the play thinner "
        ~ "than the wall)");
    assert(split > 0 && split < 1, "shadowCase: split is where base and lid meet, between 0 (the bottom) and "
        ~ "1 (the top) of the part");
    immutable n = on.normal, o = on.origin;

    // how far the part reaches along the normal, from the plane: its box once turned so the normal is Z
    immutable square = abs(n.z) > 0.999999;
    immutable b = square ? inside.bbox
        : inside
            .rotate(acos(n.z), axis: axis(origin: vec(0.mm, 0.mm, 0.mm), direction: cross(n, Z).normalized))
            .bbox;
    immutable low = (square && n.z < 0 ? -b.max.z : b.min.z) - dot(o, n);
    immutable high = (square && n.z < 0 ? -b.min.z : b.max.z) - dot(o, n);
    immutable cut = low + split * (high - low), top = high + clearance;

    // the lip as high as asked, or 3 mm where that leaves the lid's walls half the room above it
    immutable room = top - cut - play;
    immutable h = lip > 0.mm ? lip : min(3.mm, room / 2);
    assert(cut + h + play < top, "shadowCase: the lip reaches the lid's top: a shorter lip, or split lower");
    immutable bead = close == "snap" ? min(0.4.mm, wall / 4) : 0.mm;
    assert(h > 2 * bead + play, "shadowCase: the lip is too low for a snap's bead: close: \"lip\", or split lower");

    // the outline: the shadow grown, its convex hull where it is not convex; the walls drawn as rings in
    // the plane and extruded across it, from where they go
    immutable projected = inside.projection(on), hullOf = hull(projected);
    immutable shadow = hullOf.area - projected.outer.area < 1e-6 * hullOf.area ? projected.outer : hullOf;
    Profile around(Length by) => by > 0.mm ? shadow.offset(by) : shadow;
    Solid along(Profile p, Length from, Length height) => p.extrude(height).move(n * from);
    immutable outer = around(clearance + wall), inner = around(clearance);

    // the layers below overlap where they are joined: faces that meet on a slanted plane are not
    // exactly on each other, and joining them is slow and comes out broken.
    // The base: floor, walls up to the cut (from the floor's bottom), the lip on their inner half
    auto floor = along(outer, low - wall, wall);
    floor.faces.normal(n).addTag("enclosures.floor");
    auto side = along(outer - inner, low - wall, cut - low + wall);
    side.faces.normal(n).addTag("enclosures.rim");

    // the lid: the outer half of the wall round the lip (play wider), the whole wall above it, the top
    immutable over = top - cut - h - play;
    auto walls = along(outer - inner, cut + h + play, over + wall / 2);
    auto cap = along(outer, top, wall);

    // the lip and the lid's skirt round it: with snap, halfway up, a bead `bead` out from the lip and a
    // groove as much (and play) into the skirt (a step that small prints without support)
    immutable lipOut = clearance + wall / 2 - play / 2;
    immutable mid = cut + h / 2;
    auto ring = along(around(lipOut) - inner, cut - (cut - low) / 2, h + (cut - low) / 2);
    auto skirt = along(outer - around(lipOut + play), cut, h + play + over / 2);
    if (bead > 0.mm)
    {
        ring += along(around(lipOut + bead) - around((clearance + lipOut) / 2), mid - bead, 2 * bead);
        skirt -= along(around(lipOut + bead + play) - around(lipOut), mid - bead - play / 2, 2 * bead + play);
    }
    ring.addTag("enclosures.lip", recursive: true);
    auto base = floor + side + ring, lid = skirt + walls + cap;
    return Enclosure(base, lid);
}
```

## Library source: joints

```d
module joints;

/// Tags: on both pieces, the faces left by the cut (in its plane) are tagged
/// "joints.cut", and the plane itself "joints.plane" (piece.plane("joints.plane")).

/// `s` with its faces lying in the plane `p` tagged "joints.cut", and the plane "joints.plane".
private Solid cutTagged(Solid s, Plane p)
{
    bool on(Face f) => abs(dot(f.center - p.origin, p.normal)) < 0.001.mm && abs(dot(f.normal, p.normal)) > 0.999;
    // (a joint can leave no face whole in the plane: a finger joint's cut is all fingers)
    if (s.faces.filter(f => on(f)).count > 0)
        s.faces.filter(f => on(f)).addTag("joints.cut");
    return s.addTag("joints.plane", at: p);
}

/// The two pieces of a solid cut along a plane with a joint between them,
/// and the loose parts that lock it (a wedge), if any.
struct Joint
{
    Solid a;        /// the piece behind the plane (against its normal)
    Solid b;        /// the piece in front of it (where the normal points)
    Solid[] loose;  /// a wedge or dowels to print apart, in place
    Solid[] print;  /// the same lying flat on z = 0 in a row beside the body, to print
}

/// The kinds of joint splitJoint() knows.
immutable string[] jointKinds = ["tenon", "dovetail", "pins", "fingers", "lap", "kama", "kanawa", "koshikake", "barbed",
    "dowels"];

/// What a joint pushes across the plane, in the plane's own frame (x and y
/// in the plane, z along its normal), `s` its size and `g` added all round
/// (the clearance, for the hollow it fits in): `up` what piece a pushes into
/// b (z > 0), `down` what b pushes into a (z < 0).
private struct Keys
{
    Solid up;
    Solid down;
}

/// A box from (x0, y0, z0) to (x1, y1, z1), grown by g all round.
private Solid span(Length x0, Length x1, Length y0, Length y1, Length z0, Length z1, Length g) =>
    box(x1 - x0 + 2 * g, y1 - y0 + 2 * g, z1 - z0 + 2 * g)
        .move(x: (x0 + x1) / 2, y: (y0 + y1) / 2, z: z0 - g);

/// A prism across the whole piece along y, its outline in x and z.
private Solid acrossY(Vec2[] xz, Length reach) =>
    polygon(xz).extrude(2 * reach, along: Y).move(y: -reach);

/// `across`: how wide the section is along x, which the fingers share.
private Keys jointKeys(string kind, Length s, Length len, Length g, int count, Length across)
{
    // far enough to cross the whole section, whatever its shape
    immutable far = 4 * s;
    Solid none = box(0.01.mm, 0.01.mm, 0.01.mm).move(z: -10 * s - 1.mm);
    switch (kind)
    {
    case "tenon":
        {
            // a rectangular tenon, its tip chamfered to find its mortise
            immutable w = 0.5 * s, t = 0.3 * s, c = min(0.1 * t, 1.mm);
            Solid tenon = span(-w / 2, w / 2, -t / 2, t / 2, -0.01.mm, len, g);
            if (g == 0.mm)
                tenon = tenon.chamfer(edges.of(faces.top), d: c);
            return Keys(tenon, none);
        }
    case "pins":
        {
            // `count` round pins in a row along x: stout (a third of the size across, at most one
            // and a half times as long as thick) and flared at their foot, where a pin printed
            // standing up would snap along a layer; their holes get the same flare as a mouth
            // as thick as `count` of them allow in a row across 0.85 of the size, flares 1.4 times
            // their width apart, a third of the size at most
            immutable n = max(1, count);
            immutable d = min(0.3 * s, 0.85 * s / (2.24 * (n - 1) + 1.6));
            immutable tall = min(len, 1.5 * d), flare = 0.3 * d;
            immutable step = n > 1 ? max(0.55 * s / (n - 1), 2.24 * d) : 0.mm;
            Solid[] pins;
            foreach (i; 0 .. n)
            {
                auto pin = cylinder(d: d + 2 * g, h: tall + g + 0.01.mm).move(z: -0.01.mm)
                    + cone(d1: d + 2 * flare + 2 * g, d2: d + 2 * g, h: flare).move(z: -0.01.mm);
                if (g == 0.mm)
                    pin = pin.chamfer(edges.of(faces.top), d: 0.12 * d);
                pins ~= pin.move(x: (i - (n - 1) / 2.0) * step);
            }
            return Keys(fuse(pins), none);
        }
    case "dovetail":
        {
            // a tail widening into b, across the piece: it slides in along y
            // and holds against pulling apart along the normal
            immutable w = 0.35 * s, flare = len * tan(12.deg);
            return Keys(acrossY([vec(-w / 2 - g, -0.01.mm), vec(w / 2 + g, -0.01.mm),
                vec(w / 2 + flare + g, len + g), vec(-w / 2 - flare - g, len + g)], far), none);
        }
    case "fingers":
        {
            // `count` fingers across the section's width along x, b's and a's in turn, as long as len.
            // The width, not the size, and nothing past it: on a plane aslant the part's sides, what
            // lies beyond the outer fingers stays with the piece it is on, where a finger there would
            // take a sliver of it, loose
            immutable n = max(count, 3), w = across / n;
            Solid[] ups, downs;
            foreach (i; 1 .. n + 1)
            {
                immutable x0 = -across / 2 - w + i * w;
                if (i % 2 == 0)
                    ups ~= span(x0, x0 + w, -far, far, -0.01.mm, len, g);
                else
                    downs ~= span(x0, x0 + w, -far, far, -len, 0.01.mm, g);
            }
            return Keys(fuse(ups), fuse(downs));
        }
    case "lap":
        {
            // a half lap: a keeps the half on -y over len, b the half on +y
            return Keys(span(-far, far, -far, 0.mm, -0.01.mm, len, g),
                span(-far, far, 0.mm, far, -len, 0.01.mm, g));
        }
    case "kama":
        {
            // a gooseneck: a neck and a head wider than it, through along y;
            // it drops into b from the side and holds against pulling apart
            immutable neck = 0.25 * s, head = 0.45 * s, h = len / 3;
            return Keys(acrossY([vec(-neck / 2 - g, -0.01.mm), vec(neck / 2 + g, -0.01.mm),
                vec(neck / 2 + g, len - h - g), vec(head / 2 + g, len - h - g),
                vec(head / 2 + g, len + g), vec(-head / 2 - g, len + g),
                vec(-head / 2 - g, len - h - g), vec(-neck / 2 - g, len - h - g)], far), none);
        }
    case "kanawa":
        {
            // a half lap with a hook at each end that holds the two against
            // pulling apart; a wedge through the middle keeps them together
            immutable hook = 0.2 * s, lip = min(0.15 * len, 0.3 * s);
            auto up = span(-far, far, -far, 0.mm, -0.01.mm, len, g)
                + span(-far, far, -0.01.mm, hook, len - lip, len, g);
            auto down = span(-far, far, 0.mm, far, -len, 0.01.mm, g)
                + span(-far, far, -hook, 0.01.mm, -len, -len + lip, g);
            return Keys(up, down);
        }
    case "koshikake":
        {
            // a dovetail in the upper part and, under it, a seat: b's lower part runs on under a,
            // and a rests on it, so the joint carries a load without bending open
            immutable w = 0.35 * s, flare = len * tan(12.deg), seatTop = -0.15 * s, seat = 0.5 * len;
            auto tail = acrossY([vec(-w / 2 - g, -0.01.mm), vec(w / 2 + g, -0.01.mm),
                vec(w / 2 + flare + g, len + g), vec(-w / 2 - flare - g, len + g)], far);
            return Keys(tail & span(-far, far, seatTop, far, -far, far, g),
                span(-far, far, -far, seatTop, -seat, 0.01.mm, g));
        }
    case "barbed":
        {
            // a tenon with barbs, driven in: each tooth leans towards the tip (it slides in) and
            // has a flat back (it does not pull out); a slot down its middle lets the barbs close as
            // they go in and open behind the teeth they pass
            immutable w = 0.3 * s, barb = 0.05 * s, teeth = 3, seg = len / teeth;
            Vec2[] right;
            foreach (k; 0 .. teeth)
            {
                right ~= vec(w / 2, k * seg);
                right ~= vec(w / 2 + barb, k * seg + 0.01.mm);
            }
            right ~= vec(w / 2, len);
            Vec2[] outline = [vec(-w / 2, -0.01.mm), vec(w / 2, -0.01.mm)] ~ right[1 .. $];
            foreach_reverse (q; right[1 .. $])
                outline ~= vec(-q.x, q.y);
            auto shape = polygon(outline);
            if (g > 0.mm)
                shape = shape.offset(g);
            else
                shape = shape - rect(0.3 * w, 0.6 * len).move(y: len - 0.3 * len + 0.01.mm);
            return Keys(shape.extrude(2 * far, along: Y).move(y: -far), none);
        }
    case "dowels":
        // loose: the dowels and their sockets are made by dowels(), the pieces push nothing
        return Keys(none, none);
    default:
        assert(false, "the joint kind is one of tenon, dovetail, pins, fingers, lap, kama, kanawa, koshikake, barbed, "
            ~ "dowels, not " ~ kind);
    }
}

/// Loose dowels of a "dowels" joint and their sockets, in the joint's frame (x across, y the dowel's
/// thickness, z along the normal, the plane at z = 0).
private struct Dowels
{
    Solid[] pins;
    Solid[] sockets;
}

/// `count` dowels in a row along x, each `2 len` long across the plane: a round rod with two flats
/// (it prints lying on one), each end split down its middle and pointed; `grip` thicker than its
/// socket across the split, so the halves press on the socket's wall. The sockets: plain round holes
/// `g` larger than the dowel's diameter, a little deeper than it goes, chamfered at the mouth.
private Dowels dowels(Length s, Length len, Length g, int count, Length grip = 0.2.mm)
{
    immutable n = max(1, count);
    immutable d = min(0.3 * s, 0.85 * s / (1.6 * n)), t = 0.75 * d;
    immutable step = n > 1 ? max(0.55 * s / (n - 1), 1.6 * d) : 0.mm;
    immutable rod = d + g + grip, point = 0.15 * d;
    // the rod along z, its flats facing ±y, pointed at both ends
    auto pin = (cylinder(d: rod, h: 2 * len, center: true)
            & box(rod, t, 2 * len + 1.mm).move(z: -len - 0.5.mm))
        .chamfer(edges.filter(e => abs(e.mid.z) > len - 0.01.mm), d: point);
    // the splits, through the flats, from each tip to 0.4 of the way back
    immutable sw = max(0.25 * d, 0.6.mm), sl = 0.6 * len;
    auto split = box(sw, 2 * t, sl + 0.01.mm).move(z: len - sl);
    pin = pin - split - split.mirror(Z);
    // the socket: round, the dowel's diameter and the play, 0.3 mm deeper, its mouth chamfered
    immutable hole = d + g, lip = 0.4.mm;
    auto socket = cylinder(d: hole, h: 2 * (len + 0.3.mm), center: true)
        + cone(d1: hole + 2 * lip, d2: hole, h: lip)
        + cone(d1: hole + 2 * lip, d2: hole, h: lip).mirror(Z);
    Dowels r;
    foreach (i; 0 .. n)
    {
        immutable x = (i - (n - 1) / 2.0) * step;
        r.pins ~= pin.move(x: x);
        r.sockets ~= socket.move(x: x);
    }
    return r;
}

/// The loose parts of a joint (in place) laid flat on z = 0, in a row along x beyond `body`'s box.
private Solid[] flatRow(Solid[] loose, Solid body)
{
    Solid[] r;
    auto bb = body.bbox;
    Length x = bb.max.x + 10.mm;
    foreach (p; loose)
    {
        // on its largest face (of the two alike, a flat part has, the first), then along the row
        auto down = p.faces.largest.list[0].normal;
        auto laid = p.placeOn(World, from: faces.normal(down).largest);
        auto lb = laid.bbox;
        r ~= laid.move(x: x - lb.min.x, y: bb.center.y - lb.center.y);
        x += lb.size.x + 5.mm;
    }
    return r;
}

/// How far to turn a joint in the frame of plane `here` so it lies along the
/// section's longer side: a tenon's width, the way a dovetail slides.
private Angle alongLonger(Profile section, Plane here, string kind)
{
    // a dovetail and a gooseneck slide along the frame's y: that way along the longer side
    // the frame's x and y, read from a thin bar placed along each
    auto xd = box(10.mm, 0.001.mm, 0.001.mm).placeOn(here).bbox.size / 10.mm;
    auto yd = box(0.001.mm, 10.mm, 0.001.mm).placeOn(here).bbox.size / 10.mm;
    auto size = section.bbox.size;
    immutable longerY = dot(size, yd) > dot(size, xd) + 0.01.mm;
    immutable slides = kind == "dovetail" || kind == "kama" || kind == "koshikake" || kind == "barbed";
    return longerY != slides ? 90.deg : 0.deg;
}

/// `body` cut along the plane `at` into two pieces that fit together with a
/// joint, `clearance` apart where they meet (0.2 mm suits most FDM printers:
/// see the fits guide). The joint is centred on the cut (the middle of the
/// section), laid along the section's longer side; `turn` turns it further
/// about the plane's normal; `size` sets its scale
/// (by default the square root of the section's area: the width of a square
/// beam) and `length` how far it reaches across the plane (0.6 of the size).
/// `count` (or `keys`, as in splitFlat and mold) is the number of fingers,
/// pins or dowels (pins thinner the more there are). The fingers share the
/// section's width; pins and dowels go in a row across its middle or, where
/// that is hollow (a tube), on the material round it, as thick as it has
/// room for; a tenon there is an error.
///
/// - "tenon": a tenon on a, its mortise in b (hozo);
/// - "dovetail": a tail across the piece, sliding in sideways (ari);
/// - "pins": round pins on a, holes in b;
/// - "fingers": a box joint, fingers of a and b in turn;
/// - "lap": a half lap (ai-gaki), each piece keeping half the thickness;
/// - "kama": a gooseneck, dropping in from the side (kama tsugi);
/// - "kanawa": a half lap with hooks at both ends, locked by a wedge driven
///   through the middle (kanawa tsugi): the wedge is in `loose`;
/// - "koshikake": a dovetail over a seat that the other piece rests on
///   (koshikake ari tsugi), which carries a load without bending open;
/// - "barbed": a tenon with barbs, split down its middle, driven in: it goes
///   in and does not come out.
/// - "dowels": `count` loose dowels, the printed kind of wooden ones: a rod
///   with two flats, each end split, half into a round hole of a and half
///   into one of b, held by friction (the split halves press on the walls);
///   they print lying on a flat (`print`), and the holes are plain round ones.
Joint splitJoint(Solid body, Plane at, string kind = "tenon", Length size = 0.mm, Length length = 0.mm,
    Length clearance = 0.2.mm, Angle turn = 0.deg, int count = 2, int keys = -1)
{
    immutable many = keys >= 0 ? keys : count;
    auto section = body.section(at);
    immutable s = size > 0.mm ? size : sqrt(section.area);
    immutable len = length > 0.mm ? length : 0.6 * s;

    // the joint's frame: on the plane, at the middle of the section
    auto here = plane(origin: section.bbox.center, normal: at.normal);
    immutable spin = turn + alongLonger(section, here, kind);
    Solid placed(Solid k) => k.rotate(z: spin).placeOn(here);

    immutable wide = widthAlong(section, here, spin);
    auto exact = jointKeys(kind, s, len, 0.mm, many, wide);
    auto room = jointKeys(kind, s, len, clearance, many, wide);
    auto up = placed(exact.up), down = placed(exact.down);
    auto upRoom = placed(room.up), downRoom = placed(room.down);

    // what goes through both pieces (a wedge's hole, the dowels' sockets), and the loose parts
    Solid[] holes, loose;

    // a tenon or a row of pins must stand on material where it crosses the plane (its foot, half a
    // millimetre each side): in the middle of a hollow part (a tube) or a narrow one, a tenon goes
    // nowhere, and the pins go on the material round it instead
    auto slab = box(8 * s, 8 * s, 1.mm).move(z: -0.5.mm).placeOn(here);
    bool onMaterial(Solid k) => (body & k & slab).volume >= 0.99 * (k & slab).volume;
    assert(kind != "tenon" || onMaterial(up), "splitJoint: the part is hollow or narrow in the middle of the "
        ~ "cut, where the tenon goes: kind: \"pins\" or \"dowels\" (they go where the material is), or a "
        ~ "smaller size:");
    if (kind == "pins" && !onMaterial(up))
    {
        auto p = spotsFor(section, many, s, clearance, true);
        auto one = jointKeys("pins", p.size, len, 0.mm, 1, wide);
        auto oneRoom = jointKeys("pins", p.size, len, clearance, 1, wide);
        Solid[] pins, rooms;
        foreach (q; p.at)
        {
            auto there = plane(origin: q, normal: at.normal);
            pins ~= one.up.rotate(z: spin).placeOn(there);
            rooms ~= oneRoom.up.rotate(z: spin).placeOn(there);
        }
        up = fuse(pins);
        upRoom = fuse(rooms);
    }
    if (kind == "kanawa")
    {
        // the wedge: square, tapering 1 in 20, through both halves in the
        // middle of the joint, on the cut, where the two hooks pull against
        // each other; its hole is left the clearance larger. The
        // wedge goes in narrow end first: seated, that end lies flush with
        // the piece's side, the wide end stands out 3 mm to tap it home and
        // pull it out
        immutable w = 0.18 * s, reach = 2 * s, taper = reach / 20;

        // the piece's thickness the way the wedge goes through
        immutable through = widthAlong(section, here, spin + 90.deg), head = 3.mm;
        Length thick(Length z) => w + taper * (z + reach / 2) / reach;
        auto wedge = loft([rect(thick(-through / 2), thick(-through / 2)).move(z: -through / 2),
                rect(thick(through / 2 + head), thick(through / 2 + head)).move(z: through / 2 + head)])
            .rotate(x: -90);
        auto hole = loft([rect(w + 2 * clearance, w + 2 * clearance).move(z: -reach / 2),
                rect(w + taper + 2 * clearance, w + taper + 2 * clearance).move(z: reach / 2)])
            .rotate(x: -90);
        holes ~= placed(hole);
        loose ~= placed(wedge);
    }
    if (kind == "dowels")
    {
        auto d = dowels(s, len, clearance, many);
        if (onMaterial(fuse(d.sockets.map(k => placed(k)))))
        {
            holes ~= d.sockets.map(k => placed(k));
            loose ~= d.pins.map(k => placed(k));
        }
        else
        {
            // the row would leave the material: one dowel on each spot of it, as thick as it has room for
            auto p = spotsFor(section, many, s, clearance, false);
            auto one = dowels(p.size, length > 0.mm ? len : 0.6 * p.size, clearance, 1);
            foreach (q; p.at)
            {
                auto there = plane(origin: q, normal: at.normal);
                holes ~= one.sockets[0].rotate(z: spin).placeOn(there);
                loose ~= one.pins[0].rotate(z: spin).placeOn(there);
            }
        }
    }
    auto sides = body.halves(here);

    // WORKAROUND (OpenCascade 7.9, boolean cut): a kanawa's wedge hole cut from a piece of a tube once
    // its parts are joined fails (AcquiredSelfIntersection); cut from each part before, it does not.
    // tests.d tries the joined cut, on splitJoint(tube, …, kind: "kanawa")
    Solid drilled(Solid piece) => holes.length > 0 ? piece - holes : piece;
    auto a = drilled(cutTagged(sides.below, here) - downRoom) + drilled(body & up);
    auto b = drilled(cutTagged(sides.above, here) - upRoom) + drilled(body & down);
    return Joint(a, b, loose, flatRow(loose, body));
}

/// How wide the section is along the joint's x, turned by `spin` in the plane `here`: its box's reach
/// that way (a little more than the section's own where it lies aslant).
private Length widthAlong(Profile section, Plane here, Angle spin)
{
    auto kx = box(10.mm, 0.001.mm, 0.001.mm).rotate(z: spin).placeOn(here).bbox.size / 10.mm;
    return dot(section.bbox.size, kx);
}

/// Where pins or dowels go, and the size each is made for (0.3 of it across).
private struct Spots
{
    Vec3[] at;
    Length size;
}

/// Where `n` pins or dowels go on a section whose middle would leave them in the air (a tube's): on
/// its material, as far apart as they can be, each made for the size `s`, smaller until they find
/// room, the flared foot of a pin (the chamfered mouth of a dowel's socket) and 0.4 mm of wall round
/// them.
private Spots spotsFor(Profile section, int n, Length s, Length g, bool pin)
{
    Length margin(Length size) => (pin ? 0.24 * size + g : 0.15 * size + g / 2 + 0.4.mm) + 0.4.mm;
    Length size = s;
    auto at = section.spots(max(1, n), margin: margin(size));
    while (at.length < max(1, n) && size > 5.mm)
    {
        size = max(5.mm, 0.85 * size);
        at = section.spots(max(1, n), margin: margin(size));
    }
    assert(at.length > 0, "splitJoint: the part's walls are too thin at the cut for " ~ (pin ? "pins" : "dowels")
        ~ ": kind: \"lap\" or \"fingers\"");
    return Spots(at, size);
}

/// The two halves of a solid cut flat along a plane, each to print lying on
/// its cut face, and the flat keys that join them.
struct FlatSplit
{
    Solid a;        /// the half behind the plane (against its normal)
    Solid b;        /// the half in front of it
    Solid[] keys;   /// the keys, in place, where they go
    Solid aPrint;   /// a, lying on its cut face on z = 0, to print
    Solid bPrint;   /// b, the same
    Solid[] print;  /// the keys lying flat on z = 0 in a row beside the body, to print
}

/// The outline of a key, along x, `len` long, centred on the origin.
private Profile keyOutline(string kind, Length len)
{
    switch (kind)
    {
    case "bowtie":
        {
            // a butterfly (chigiri): wide ends, a narrow waist
            immutable wide = 0.6 * len, waist = 0.3 * len;
            return polygon([vec(-len / 2, -wide / 2), vec(0.mm, -waist / 2), vec(len / 2, -wide / 2),
                    vec(len / 2, wide / 2), vec(0.mm, waist / 2), vec(-len / 2, wide / 2)])
                .round(min(1.mm, 0.08 * len));
        }
    case "disc":
        return circle(d: 0.6 * len);
    default:
        assert(false, "the key kind is bowtie or disc, not " ~ kind);
    }
}

/// `body` cut flat along the plane `at` into two halves, each printed lying
/// on its cut face (nothing stands out of it, so it lies flat on the bed),
/// joined by `keys` flat keys (or `count`, as in splitJoint): a pocket in
/// each half's cut face, half the key in each. The keys print lying flat
/// too, and fit their pockets `clearance` apart; glue them in, or leave them
/// dry to take apart.
///
/// The keys go where the cut has room for them, at least `wall` from its
/// edges, as far apart as they can be. "bowtie" keys (butterflies, chigiri)
/// keep the halves from sliding and from turning, even one alone; "disc"
/// keys are round, two at least. `size` is a key's length (from the
/// section's size unless given), `depth` how deep it goes into each half.
/// The pockets open with a 0.4 mm chamfer: the first layers spread a little
/// on the bed, and the pocket's mouth is on the bed.
FlatSplit splitFlat(Solid body, Plane at, int keys = 2, string kind = "bowtie", Length size = 0.mm,
    Length depth = 0.mm, Length clearance = 0.15.mm, Length wall = 1.6.mm, int count = -1)
{
    immutable many = count >= 0 ? count : keys;
    assert(many >= 1, "splitFlat needs one key at least");
    auto section = body.section(at);

    // the keys' length: given, or from the section's size, smaller until they find room in it
    // (half their length, half their width for a disc, and the wall, from its edges)
    Length len = size > 0.mm ? size : clamp(0.3 * sqrt(section.area), 8.mm, 30.mm);
    Length room(Length l) => (kind == "disc" ? 0.3 : 0.5) * l + wall;
    auto spots = section.spots(many, margin: room(len));
    while (spots.length == 0 && size == 0.mm && len > 4.mm)
    {
        len = max(4.mm, 0.8 * len);
        spots = section.spots(many, margin: room(len));
    }
    assert(spots.length > 0, "splitFlat: the cut has no room for a key $(len) long $(wall) from its edges: "
        ~ "a smaller size: or wall:");
    immutable d = depth > 0.mm ? depth : clamp(0.25 * len, 2.mm, 6.mm);
    immutable thick = 2 * d - 0.3.mm;
    auto outline = keyOutline(kind, len);

    // the pocket through both halves at the cut, its mouth chamfered both ways
    immutable lip = 0.4.mm;
    auto mouth = outline.offset(clearance + lip).extrude(lip, taper: 45.deg);
    auto pocket = outline.offset(clearance).extrude(2 * d).move(z: -d)
        + mouth + mouth.mirror(Z);
    auto key = outline.extrude(thick)
        .chamfer(edges.of(faces.top) + edges.of(faces.bottom), d: 0.3.mm);

    Solid[] pockets, placed, flat;
    auto bb = body.bbox;
    foreach (i, p; spots)
    {
        auto here = plane(origin: p, normal: at.normal);
        pockets ~= pocket.placeOn(here);
        placed ~= key.move(z: -thick / 2).placeOn(here);
        flat ~= key.move(x: bb.max.x + 10.mm + len / 2 + i * (len + 5.mm), y: bb.center.y);
    }
    auto sides = body.halves(at);
    auto a = cutTagged(sides.below, at) - pockets;
    auto b = cutTagged(sides.above, at) - pockets;

    // each half on its cut face: the face lying in the plane, facing out of the half
    bool cutFace(Face f, Vec3 n) =>
        dot(f.normal, n) > 0.999 && abs(dot(f.center - at.origin, at.normal)) < 0.001.mm;
    auto aPrint = a.placeOn(World, from: faces.filter(f => cutFace(f, at.normal)));
    auto bPrint = b.placeOn(World, from: faces.filter(f => cutFace(f, -at.normal)));
    return FlatSplit(a, b, placed, aPrint, bPrint, flat);
}

/// Two separate parts joined where one meets the other: `b` ends on the plane
/// `at` (a face of `a`, its normal pointing into `b`), and the joint goes from
/// `b` into `a`: a shelf into an upright, a rail into a post. The joint is
/// centred on `b`'s end and sized by it, as splitJoint does; what reaches past
/// `a`'s far side stops flush with it (a through tenon). Kinds: "tenon",
/// "dovetail" (a sliding dovetail, its housing running out of `a` the way it
/// slides in), "pins", "fingers" (a corner of a box), "lap", "kama" (its
/// housing too runs out of `a`), "koshikake" (a sliding dovetail over a
/// seat, its housing running out of `a` too), "barbed" (driven in for good),
/// "dowels" (holes in both, the dowels in `.loose` and, lying flat, in
/// `.print`); not "kanawa", which joins two ends: splitJoint. `count` (or
/// `keys`) as in splitJoint. Gives the two parts changed: `.a` with the
/// hollows, `.b` with what fits in them.
Joint joinParts(Solid a, Solid b, Plane at, string kind = "tenon", Length size = 0.mm, Length length = 0.mm,
    Length clearance = 0.2.mm, Angle turn = 0.deg, int count = 2, int keys = -1)
{
    assert(kind != "kanawa", "joinParts joins two parts that meet; a wedged scarf joins two ends: splitJoint");
    immutable many = keys >= 0 ? keys : count;
    // b's end, a hair inside it
    auto end = b.section(plane(origin: at.origin + at.normal * 0.01.mm, normal: at.normal));
    immutable s = size > 0.mm ? size : sqrt(end.area);
    immutable slides = kind == "dovetail" || kind == "kama" || kind == "koshikake";

    // a's depth behind the plane: a housing that runs out of a the way it slides must stop short
    // of a's far side, or it cuts a in two
    auto ab = a.bbox;
    Length deep = 0.mm;
    foreach (x; [ab.min.x, ab.max.x])
        foreach (y; [ab.min.y, ab.max.y])
            foreach (z; [ab.min.z, ab.max.z])
                deep = max(deep, dot(at.origin - vec(x, y, z), at.normal));
    Length len = length > 0.mm ? length : 0.6 * s;
    if (slides)
        len = min(len, 0.6 * deep);

    // the joint's frame on the plane, in the middle of b's end, its z going into a
    auto here = plane(origin: end.bbox.center - at.normal * 0.01.mm, normal: -at.normal);
    immutable spin = turn + alongLonger(end, here, kind);
    Solid placed(Solid k) => k.rotate(z: spin).placeOn(here);
    immutable wide = widthAlong(end, here, spin);
    auto exact = jointKeys(kind, s, len, 0.mm, many, wide);
    auto room = jointKeys(kind, s, len, clearance, many, wide);

    // what one pushes into the other stays within b's end, carried across the plane both ways
    auto footprint = end.extrude(2 * (len + 1.mm), symmetric: true);
    // a dovetail's or a gooseneck's housing runs on along the way it slides, out of a, so b goes in
    auto housing = slides ? placed(room.up) : placed(room.up) & footprint.offset(clearance, sharp: true);
    auto na = a - housing + (b & placed(exact.down) & footprint);
    auto nb = b + (a & placed(exact.up) & footprint) - placed(room.down);
    Solid[] loose;
    if (kind == "dowels")
    {
        auto d = dowels(s, len, clearance, many);
        na -= d.sockets.map(k => placed(k));
        nb -= d.sockets.map(k => placed(k));
        loose ~= d.pins.map(k => placed(k));
    }
    return Joint(cutTagged(na, at), cutTagged(nb, at), loose, flatRow(loose, a + b));
}
```

## Library source: molds

```d
module molds;

/// The two halves of a mold, where they go and laid for printing.
///
/// Tags: the faces of the hollow the object leaves are "molds.cavity", the
/// halves' faces along the parting plane "molds.parting", the pour hole's
/// "molds.sprue".
struct Mold
{
    Solid a;        /// the half behind the parting plane (against its normal), with the keys and the seal
    Solid b;        /// the half in front of it, with the pour hole and the vents
    Solid aPrint;   /// a on its outer face on z = 0, the parting face up
    Solid bPrint;   /// b the same
}

/// A two-part mold to cast `object` in (silicone, resin, plaster): a block
/// `wall` thick round it, cut along the parting plane `at`, the object's
/// shape hollow inside. The plane should cross the object where it is widest,
/// so each half lets go of the cast.
///
/// - `keys` (or `count`, as in splitJoint) cones on a's parting face and
///   their sockets in b's line the halves up (where the face has room, as
///   far apart as they can be), `clearance` apart;
/// - a seal round the cavity (its convex hull), a ridge `seal` high on a and its groove in b,
///   keeps the liquid from creeping out between the halves (0.mm: none);
/// - a pour hole `sprue` wide with a funnel, and `vents` thin channels for the
///   air, go up through b from the cavity's highest points (along the plane's
///   normal: put that side up when pouring).
///
/// - `pry`: a notch on two opposite sides, across the parting line, to open
///   the mold with a flat screwdriver without marring its faces.
///
/// Both halves print with the parting face up, on their outer faces
/// (`aPrint`, `bPrint`): the keys and the seal stand up, the sockets and the
/// groove open upwards, with no supports.
Mold mold(Solid object, Plane at, Length wall = 10.mm, int keys = 4, Length sprue = 6.mm, int vents = 2,
    Length seal = 0.8.mm, Length clearance = 0.15.mm, bool pry = true, int count = -1)
{
    immutable many = count >= 0 ? count : keys;
    immutable n = at.normal;
    auto bb = object.bbox;

    // the block square to the parting plane: the object's box measured along the plane's own axes
    // (read from a speck laid on it along each), grown by the wall, built there and placed on the plane
    auto centre = plane(origin: bb.center - n * dot(bb.center - at.origin, n), normal: n);
    Vec3 axis(Solid speck) => (speck.placeOn(centre).bbox.center - centre.origin).normalized;
    auto xd = axis(box(0.001.mm, 0.001.mm, 0.001.mm).move(x: 10.mm));
    auto yd = axis(box(0.001.mm, 0.001.mm, 0.001.mm).move(y: 10.mm));
    Vec3[] corners;
    foreach (x; [bb.min.x, bb.max.x])
        foreach (y; [bb.min.y, bb.max.y])
            foreach (z; [bb.min.z, bb.max.z])
                corners ~= vec(x, y, z) - centre.origin;
    // how far the object reaches along d from the centre: between where its box's corners say, halved
    // until what of the object lies beyond is gone
    immutable big = 4 * bb.size.length + 10.mm;
    immutable square = abs(n.x) > 0.9999 || abs(n.y) > 0.9999 || abs(n.z) > 0.9999;
    Length extent(Vec3 d)
    {
        Length inside = corners.map(c => dot(c, d)).minElement, outside = corners.map(c => dot(c, d)).maxElement;
        // a plane square to an axis: the box is the object's own, along the frame's axes too
        if (square)
            return outside;
        foreach (k; 0 .. 14)
        {
            immutable mid = (inside + outside) / 2;
            auto past = box(big, big, big).placeOn(plane(origin: centre.origin + d * mid, normal: d));
            if ((object & past).volume > 0.001 * 1.mm ^^ 3)
                inside = mid;
            else
                outside = mid;
        }
        return outside;
    }
    immutable hx = extent(xd), lx = -extent(-xd), hy = extent(yd), ly = -extent(-yd), hn = extent(n), ln = -extent(-n);
    Length lo(Vec3 d) => d == xd ? lx : d == yd ? ly : ln;
    Length hi(Vec3 d) => d == xd ? hx : d == yd ? hy : hn;
    auto block = box(hi(xd) - lo(xd) + 2 * wall, hi(yd) - lo(yd) + 2 * wall, hi(n) - lo(n) + 2 * wall)
        .move(x: (hi(xd) + lo(xd)) / 2, y: (hi(yd) + lo(yd)) / 2, z: lo(n) - wall)
        .fillet(edges.parallel(Z), r: wall / 2)
        .placeOn(centre);
    auto sides = (block - object.addTag("molds.cavity", recursive: true)).halves(at);
    Solid a = sides.below, b = sides.above;
    bool parting(Face f) => abs(dot(f.center - at.origin, n)) < 0.001.mm && abs(dot(f.normal, n)) > 0.999;
    if (a.faces.filter(f => parting(f)).count > 0)
        a.faces.filter(f => parting(f)).addTag("molds.parting");
    if (b.faces.filter(f => parting(f)).count > 0)
        b.faces.filter(f => parting(f)).addTag("molds.parting");

    // the keys: truncated cones, half as high as they are wide at the foot, on the parting face round
    // the cavity, clear of the edges and of the seal
    immutable kd = clamp(0.35 * wall, 3.mm, 8.mm), kh = kd / 2;
    auto key = cone(d1: kd, d2: kd / 2, h: kh) + cylinder(d: kd, h: 0.01.mm).move(z: -0.01.mm);
    auto socket = cone(d1: kd + 2 * clearance, d2: kd / 2 + 2 * clearance, h: kh + clearance)
        .move(z: -0.01.mm);
    // the seal runs round the cavity's convex hull (an outline grown that far round a concave
    // cavity would overlap itself across its notches); the keys stay outside the seal
    auto rim = hull(object.section(at));
    auto face = block.section(at) - (seal > 0.mm ? rim.offset(1.5.mm + seal + clearance) : rim);
    immutable clear = kd / 2 + 1.5.mm;
    Solid[] knobs, holes;
    auto spots = face.spots(many, margin: clear);
    assert(spots.length > 0, "mold: no room for the keys on the parting face: a thicker wall:");
    foreach (p; spots)
    {
        auto here = plane(origin: p, normal: n);
        knobs ~= key.placeOn(here);
        holes ~= socket.placeOn(here);
    }
    a = a + fuse(knobs);
    b = b - holes;

    // the seal: a ridge round the cavity, 1.5 mm out from it, as wide as it is high, and its groove
    if (seal > 0.mm)
    {
        // each outline extruded on its own, then one less the other (a ring extruded in a slanted
        // plane comes out broken); the ridge starts a little inside a, so the two do not merely meet
        // on the parting face (a fuse on a slanted face that they share fails)
        immutable sink = 0.05.mm;
        a = a + (rim.offset(1.5.mm + seal).extrude(seal + sink) - rim.offset(1.5.mm).extrude(seal + sink))
            .move(n * -sink);
        b = b - (rim.offset(1.5.mm + seal + clearance).extrude(seal + clearance)
            - rim.offset(1.5.mm - clearance).extrude(seal + clearance));
    }

    // the pour hole and the vents: from points just under the cavity's top, along the normal, out
    // through b; the pour hole opens into a funnel at the block's face
    immutable top = dot(centre.origin, n) + hn;
    immutable reach = top + wall - dot(at.origin, n);
    auto near = plane(origin: at.origin + n * (reach - wall - 0.3.mm), normal: n);
    auto highs = object.section(near).spots(vents + 1, margin: 0.mm);
    foreach (i, p; highs)
    {
        auto here = plane(origin: p, normal: n);
        immutable length = wall + 1.mm;
        if (i == 0)
            b = b - (cylinder(d: sprue, h: length)
                + cone(d1: sprue, d2: 2 * sprue, h: sprue / 2 + 0.01.mm).move(z: wall + 0.5.mm - sprue / 2))
                .placeOn(here)
                .addTag("molds.sprue", recursive: true);
        else
            b = b - cylinder(d: 2.mm, h: length).placeOn(here);
    }
    // the notches to pry it open: half-round, across the parting line, in the middle of two opposite
    // sides of the block (those facing X, or across the normal and Z), where the block reaches
    if (pry)
    {
        auto way = abs(n.z) > 0.9 ? X : cross(n, Z).normalized;
        auto across = abs(dot(way, xd)) >= abs(dot(way, yd)) ? xd : yd;
        auto mid = centre.origin + xd * ((hx + lx) / 2) + yd * ((hy + ly) / 2);
        immutable half = (across == xd ? hx - lx : hy - ly) / 2 + wall;
        immutable notch = clamp(0.6 * wall, 4.mm, 8.mm);
        Solid[] notches;
        foreach (side; [1, -1])
            notches ~= cylinder(d: notch, h: notch / 2 + 1.mm)
                .move(z: -notch / 2)
                .placeOn(plane(origin: mid + across * (side * half), normal: across * side));
        a = a - notches;
        b = b - notches;
    }
    return Mold(a, b, a.placeOn(World, from: faces.farthest(-n)), b.placeOn(World, from: faces.farthest(n)));
}
```

## Library source: flex

```d
module flex;

/// `body` made to bend where it lies inside `zone` (any solid: a box across
/// a plate, a ring round a tube): rows of slots through its thickness, each
/// row shifted half a slot from the next, so what is left is a lattice of thin
/// bars that twist and bend (kerf bending, as in laser-cut plywood). The slots
/// go through the part's thinnest way inside the zone, and run across the
/// body's length (along its shorter side), so it bends along its length.
/// `along:` (X, Y or Z) sets the way they run instead. The slots run along
/// the axes X, Y and Z only, and go through along one of them: make a part
/// that lies turned at an angle bend before turning it.
///
/// - `width`: how wide each slot is (0.8 mm: two lines of a 0.4 mm nozzle
///   leave it open);
/// - `bridge`: the material between two slots of a row: the narrower, the
///   softer it bends;
/// - `pitch`: from one row to the next: the closer, the tighter it bends;
/// - `length`: of each slot (six times the pitch unless given, shorter on a
///   narrow part: its width less a bridge, so there is material at its
///   ends). Slots that cut the part apart are an error.
///
/// In PLA a few degrees per row; PETG and TPU bend much further. Print the part
/// lying flat, the slots upright.
Solid kerf(Solid body, Solid zone, Length width = 0.8.mm, Length bridge = 2.mm, Length pitch = 2.5.mm,
    Length length = 0.mm, Vec3 along = vec(0, 0, 0))
{
    auto part = body & zone;
    assert(part.volume > 0.mm ^^ 3, "kerf: the zone does not meet the body");
    auto bb = part.bbox;
    auto size = bb.size;

    // which way is through (the thinnest), which along (the longest, or as given), which across
    int thin = size.x <= size.y && size.x <= size.z ? 0 : size.y <= size.z ? 1 : 2;
    int run = 0;
    if (along != vec(0, 0, 0))
    {
        run = abs(along.x) > 0.5 ? 0 : abs(along.y) > 0.5 ? 1 : 2;
        assert(run != thin, "kerf: the slots cannot run along the way they go through");
    }
    else
    {
        // across the body's length: the shorter of the other two ways of the whole body, so the part
        // bends along its length (a strip bends end to end, a tube's band lets it bow)
        auto whole = body.bbox.size;
        auto s = [whole.x / 1.mm, whole.y / 1.mm, whole.z / 1.mm];
        immutable a = (thin + 1) % 3, b = (thin + 2) % 3;
        run = s[a] <= s[b] ? a : b;
    }
    auto dims = [size.x / 1.mm, size.y / 1.mm, size.z / 1.mm];
    immutable across = 3 - thin - run;
    immutable longSide = dims[run] * 1.mm, wide = dims[across] * 1.mm, deep = dims[thin] * 1.mm;

    // six pitches, or on a narrow part (a strap) the part's width less a bridge: in every other row a
    // slot in the middle, half a bridge of material at each end, and in the rows between two from the
    // edges with a bridge between them
    immutable len = length > 0.mm ? length : min(6 * pitch, longSide - bridge);
    assert(len > 2 * width, "kerf: the zone is too narrow along the slots for slots and bridges: a wider "
        ~ "zone, or narrower bridges (bridge:)");

    // the slots as a profile: x along them, y across, then stood on the plane square to `through`
    auto region = rect(longSide + 2 * len, wide);
    auto slots = region.tiles(tile: slot(len, width), step: [vec(len + bridge, 0.mm), vec((len + bridge) / 2, pitch)],
        whole: true);

    // the profile's plane square to the thinnest way: extrude(along:) stands it across X or Y, its x along
    // the other horizontal axis (along: X) or X itself (along: Y), its y up Z; turned when the slots must
    // run the other way in that plane
    immutable h = deep + 2.mm;
    auto turned = (thin == 0 ? run == 1 : run == 0) ? slots : slots.rotate(z: 90);
    auto cutter = thin == 2 ? turned.extrude(h).move(z: -h / 2)
        : thin == 1 ? turned.extrude(h, along: Y).move(y: -h / 2)
        : turned.extrude(h, along: X).move(x: -h / 2);
    auto r = body - (cutter.move(x: bb.center.x, y: bb.center.y, z: bb.center.z) & zone);
    assert(r.pieces.length <= body.pieces.length, "kerf: the slots cut the part apart: shorter slots "
        ~ "(length:) or wider bridges (bridge:)");
    return r;
}
```

## Library source: carlo

```d
module carlo;

/// Carlo, hackerscad's mascot: a bag clip whose toothed
/// slot and keyring eye make a little crocodile. Fold
/// the top of a bag of biscuits and push it into the
/// wavy slot: the teeth hold it. The start example
/// (examples/00_carlo.hcad) shows this same code;
/// chapter 13 of the tutorial explains it.

/// Carlo lying flat on z = 0, `height` tall, the
/// slot opening towards +X. `lean` is how far the back
/// and the tips lean (the clip slides onto the bag).
/// `mouth` tilts the lower jaw: down to open the slot
/// towards the tips (it slides on more easily), up to
/// close it (it holds tighter). `eye` adds the keyring
/// eye on the top corner. Prints flat, as it comes: a
/// constrained sketch, extruded.
Solid carlo(int teeth = 3, Length height = 15.mm,
    Length toothR = 2.5.mm, Length gap = 2.9.mm,
    Length jaw = 5.mm, Length back = 5.4.mm,
    Angle lean = 17.deg, Angle mouth = 1.5.deg,
    bool eye = true)
{
    assert(teeth >= 1, "a jaw needs a tooth at least");
    auto s = sketch();

    // where the points start: near where they end up
    // (the constraints below move them into place),
    // from the rows of teeth, the top and bottom sides
    // and the slot's depth
    immutable axis = toothR + gap / 2;
    immutable top = axis + toothR + jaw;
    immutable slot = 4 * teeth * toothR;
    immutable slope = tan(lean);
    auto a = s.point(-back + top * slope, -top,
        fixed: true);
    auto b = s.point(slot + 2 * toothR, -top);
    auto c = s.point(slot - 2 * toothR, top);

    // the block: a level top, the back leaning, the
    // tips of the jaws parallel to it
    auto bottom = s.line(a, b);
    SketchLine left, topSide;
    immutable corner = -back - top * slope; // top left
    if (eye)
    {
        // the eye: a ring on the top edge, its centre
        // on the top's line, round over the corner and
        // down onto the back, touching it; where it
        // rises from the top, a small rounding (an arc
        // touching both), not a corner
        immutable eyeR = 5.mm, nook = 1.5.mm;
        immutable rise = corner + 2 * eyeR;
        auto centre = s.point(corner + eyeR, top);
        auto eyeBack = s.point(corner + 3.mm * slope,
            top - 3.mm);
        auto nookCentre = s.point(rise + 1.mm,
            top + nook);
        auto nookTop = s.point(rise + 1.mm, top);
        auto nookEye = s.point(rise - 0.3.mm,
            top + 1.mm);
        left = s.line(a, eyeBack);
        topSide = s.line(c, nookTop);
        auto ring = s.arc(centre, nookEye, eyeBack);
        auto rounding = s.arc(nookCentre, nookEye,
            nookTop);
        s.on(centre, topSide);
        s.radius(ring, eyeR);
        s.tangent(left, ring);
        s.radius(rounding, nook);
        s.tangent(topSide, rounding);
        s.tangent(ring, rounding);
        s.distance(a, centre, 2 * top, along: Y);

        // the keyring hole, in the middle of the eye
        s.circle(centre, d: 3.8.mm);
    }
    else
    {
        // no eye: the back meets the top in a corner,
        // rounded
        auto d = s.point(corner, top);
        left = s.line(a, d);
        topSide = s.line(c, d);
        s.distance(a, d, 2 * top, along: Y);
        s.fillet(d, 2.5.mm);
    }
    s.horizontal(topSide);
    s.angle(topSide, left, 90.deg - lean);

    // the two rows of teeth: semicircles of one radius,
    // end to end, pocket and tooth in turn; a row is
    // points along a line, each arc between two of
    // them, its centre on the line too. The upper row
    // is level, the lower one tilts by the mouth. The
    // first pocket of each row starts where it touches
    // the end of the slot instead, and the last tooth
    // ends where it touches the tip of its jaw
    SketchPoint[] lower, upper;
    foreach (i; 0 .. 2 * teeth + 1)
    {
        lower ~= s.point(2 * toothR * i, -axis);
        upper ~= s.point(2 * toothR * i, axis);
    }
    SketchArc firstLower, firstUpper;
    SketchArc lastLower, lastUpper;

    // the upper row's last centre: with upper[1], its
    // direction
    SketchPoint lastCentre;

    // the lower row's points and centres, put on its
    // line below
    SketchPoint[] lowerOnRow;
    foreach (k; 0 .. 2 * teeth)
    {
        immutable x = 2 * toothR * k + toothR;
        auto cl = s.point(x, -axis);
        auto cu = s.point(x, axis);

        // counter-clockwise from start to end: left to
        // right goes under, right to left goes over.
        // Lower row: pockets down, teeth up; upper row:
        // pockets up, teeth down (facing the lower
        // pockets)
        auto pl = k % 2 == 0
            ? s.arc(cl, lower[k], lower[k + 1])
            : s.arc(cl, lower[k + 1], lower[k]);
        auto pu = k % 2 == 0
            ? s.arc(cu, upper[k + 1], upper[k])
            : s.arc(cu, upper[k], upper[k + 1]);
        s.radius(pl, toothR);
        s.radius(pu, toothR);

        // each centre on its row; the upper row level
        immutable onRow = k == 0 ? k + 1 : k;
        lowerOnRow ~= cl;
        if (k > 1)
            lowerOnRow ~= lower[k];
        s.horizontal(upper[onRow], cu);
        if (k > 0 && k < 2 * teeth - 1)
            s.horizontal(upper[k], upper[k + 1]);
        if (k == 0)
        {
            firstLower = pl;
            firstUpper = pu;
        }
        if (k == 2 * teeth - 1)
        {
            lastLower = pl;
            lastUpper = pu;
            lastCentre = cu;
        }
    }

    // the end of the slot: parallel to the back, the
    // back's thickness behind it, touching the first
    // pocket of each row where they meet it
    auto end = s.line(lower[0], upper[0]);
    s.parallel(end, left);
    s.distance(lower[0], left, back * cos(lean));
    s.tangent(end, firstLower);
    s.tangent(end, firstUpper);

    // the rows start on the end's line, the gap apart:
    // the upper one level, the lower one tilted by the
    // mouth, down to open it, up to close it
    // (construction lines, which guide the outline
    // without being part of it)
    auto start = s.point(axis * slope, -axis);
    s.on(start, end);
    s.distance(a, start, top - axis, along: Y);
    s.distance(start, upper[1], 2 * axis, along: Y);
    auto lowerRow = s.line(start, lowerOnRow[$ - 1],
        construction: true);
    auto upperRow = s.line(upper[1], lastCentre,
        construction: true);

    // from the lower row to the upper one:
    // counter-clockwise when it opens
    s.angle(lowerRow, upperRow, mouth);
    foreach (p; lowerOnRow[0 .. $ - 1])
        s.on(p, lowerRow);
    s.on(lower[1], lowerRow);

    // the bottom drops with the lower row, from below
    // its start
    auto under = s.point(axis * slope, -top);
    s.vertical(start, under);
    s.horizontal(a, under);
    auto drop = s.line(under, b, construction: true);
    s.parallel(drop, lowerRow);

    // the tips of the jaws, parallel to the back,
    // touching the last teeth
    auto tipLow = s.line(b, lower[$ - 1]);
    auto tipUp = s.line(upper[$ - 1], c);
    s.parallel(tipLow, left);
    s.parallel(tipUp, left);
    s.tangent(tipLow, lastLower);
    s.tangent(tipUp, lastUpper);

    // round outer corners
    foreach (p; [a, b, c])
        s.fillet(p, 2.5.mm);

    return s.profile.extrude(height);
}
```
